title: Token sourcing arbitrage and routing guidelines
content:
Executive summary:

This working doc captures a playbook and quick spreadsheet snapshot for exploiting short-term price differentials ("arbitrage") across model variants, regions, and capacity types for the hosted API. The goal is operational rules that reduce average per-token cost (PPK) while protecting latency SLOs and quality guardrails. This is a pragmatic, conservative set of recommendations we can A/B in canary routing.

Key idea: route compatible requests to cheaper execution paths when the expected PPK reduction exceeds the operational friction (latency delta, quality risk, and routing complexity). We treat "cheaper execution paths" as any of: lower-cost region, reserved capacity pool, a quantized/precision-reduced model variant, or a lower-SLA SKU during surplus capacity.

Assumptions and constraints (high level):
- Quality budget: 99.5% of responses must match baseline quality thresholds (per-eval suite) for high-tier customers. For low-tier/experimental cohorts we allow up to 2% degradations if latency/cost win is material.
- Latency SLO bands: <200ms (low), 200–500ms (medium), >500ms (high). We avoid moving requests across bands unless arbitrage delta > 20% and customer tier permits.
- Model compatibility: route only when model family variant has validated token-level regression <0.5% on our evals (or explicitly indicated for experimental cohorts).
- Billing/Quota: routing is invisible to customer (same API, same token billing). Internal cost accounting will attribute tokens to final execution path.

Simple decision rule (prototype):
1) Compute expected_ppl_cost = base_ppk(model, region) * expected_tokens(seq_len_distribution)
2) Compute candidate_alternative_costs for each compatible (region/variant/pool)
3) If min(candidate_alternative_cost) <= expected_ppl_cost * (1 - threshold) and latency_penalty <= latency_budget and quality_risk <= quality_budget -> route to alternative
4) Track outcomes and auto-revert if regression or latency violations > rolling thresholds

Thresholds (initial defaults):
- threshold (minimum cost reduction): 8%
- latency_budget (allowed percentile increase): 25% on p95 for medium/low tier; 10% for latency-sensitive tier
- quality_budget: 0.5% expected eval delta for production; 1.5% for experiment cohort

Spreadsheet snapshot (example rows — paste into a sheet for simulations):

model,region,pool_type,spot_rate_usd_per_gpu_hour,reserve_rate_usd_per_gpu_hour,avg_seq_len,estimated_tokens_per_call,estimated_ppk_usd,expected_latency_p95_ms,qual_delta_pct,arbitrage_delta_pct,route_action
m-3b,us-west,spot,1.20,1.90,64,180,0.0018,180,0.2,18,route-to-spot-us-west
ft-3b-econ,eu-west,reserved,1.60,2.10,48,140,0.0015,210,0.4,25,route-to-reserved-eu-west
open-7b,us-east,quant-8bit,2.40,3.20,128,320,0.0023,350,0.6,12,maybe-route-if-tolerant
redwood-14b,us-central,dedicated,5.80,6.50,256,640,0.0070,120,0.0,-4,do-not-route

Notes on table interpretation:
- estimated_ppk_usd is a synthesized per-token cost calibrated from capacity amortization, infra egress, licensing, and cache benefits.
- arbitrage_delta_pct = (base_ppk - candidate_ppk) / base_ppk * 100; positive means cheaper. Negative means more expensive.

Operational playbook (step-by-step):
1) Canary phase (7–14d): enable routing for a single low-risk cohort (internal dev org) with a single low-impact model family. Collect metrics: p95 latency, error rate, eval-quality-sample, ppk realized.
2) Expansion: if canary shows cost reduction and no quality/latency regressions, expand to 10% of traffic across more cohorts and a 2nd region.
3) Guardrails and monitoring: create alerts on
   - p95 latency increase > configured band for any cohort
   - eval-quality drift > threshold during rolling sample
   - routing-induced errors (5xx) spiking > 0.2% absolute
4) Fallbacks: immediate fallback to baseline model/region on alert. Maintain a 30-minute manual override and a 24-hour auto-fallback if no resolution.
5) Billing transparency: update internal chargeback reports to label tokens with final execution path so finance can reconcile reserved pool utilization.

Risk matrix and mitigations:
- Quality regression: mitigate via conservative model variant whitelist and continuous sampling + human-in-loop review for flagged queries.
- Latency regressions: only route to regions with healthy network path (steady-state RTT < 70ms extra) or to reserved pools in the same region.
- Capacity churn / spot termination: route non-critical, retry-on-fallback with exponential backoff and mark sessions for re-eval to catch quality shifts.

Data needs for scoring engine (minimal):
- live per-model per-region ppk estimates (hourly)
- request-level expected tokens (lookahead based on client-provided seq_hint or historical distribution)
- model variant quality deltas per-eval-suite (weekly snapshot)
- latency mapping matrix between source-region and exec-region (p50/p95)

Quick simulation run checklist (for SRE/Optimize):
- ingest last 14 days of traffic by customer cohort and model family
- compute baseline per-call PPK and latency percentiles
- simulate routing with thresholds at 5/8/12% cost-savings and record: net tokens routed, dollar savings, incidents flagged
- produce a 48h rolling dashboard and a gating report before expansion

Action items (owners & next steps):
- Marco Silva: prototype a scheduler that returns top-3 alternatives per request (due 2026-03-15)
- Rina Das: curate model-variant whitelist and attach eval deltas (due 2026-02-28) [in progress]
- Tomás Alvarez: add routing attribution to internal billing pipeline (due 2026-03-05)
- Product Optimize: run a 2-week canary with internal traffic and circulate results to eng/product (target start 2026-03-10)

Questions for leadership:
- What is the lowest acceptable ppk reduction to justify cross-region routing for enterprise customers (we propose 12%)?
- Are we comfortable exposing a persistent 1% sample of routed traffic for manual QA review?

Appendix: short glossary
- PPK: price per thousand tokens (we also use per-token in some sheets; normalize to per-token for routing math)
- Arbitrage delta: relative cost improvement vs baseline execution path
- Reserved pool: capacity committed under our Dedicated/reserved contracts or internally allocated reserved SKUs

Raw simulation snippet (CSV) — small sample to paste into sheets for Monte Carlo: see table above.

End of doc. This is intentionally written as a working playbook; please edit in-place and add experimental results below as you run canaries.
